stem:
*Mimulus* is a plant genus containing a diverse range of species that have colourful flowers to attract pollinators, such as bees and hummingbirds. Pollinators transfer pollen between flowers for plant sexual reproduction.

Table 5.1 compares some features of two closely-related species of *Mimulus* that both grow in the same region of North America.

The features in which they differ are:

• the altitude at which the two species grow
• their flower characteristics, including petal colour and the distance from the opening of the flower to the nectar on which the pollinators feed
• the percentages of pollinator visits that they receive from bees or from hummingbirds.
